source: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 9 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 9
knowledgePattern: Linearise exponential and logarithmic unknowns while retaining their ranges
solution:
Put u=2x, v=log2y and w=log2z. The original restrictions give u>0, v>0, while w can be any real number. The three equations become ku+v+w=3, u+kv+w=2, u+v+w=k.

Subtract the third equation from the first two: (k−1)u=3−k and (k−1)v=2−k. At k = 1 the first equation is impossible. Otherwise u=(3−k)/(k−1) and v=(2−k)/(k−1).

The first quotient is positive exactly for 1<k<3, and the second exactly for 1<k<2. Their common range is therefore 1<k<2.

Conversely any k in that range gives positive u,v and real w=k−u−v. Taking x=log2u, y=2v>1 and z=2w>0 supplies a valid solution. Thus the range is necessary and sufficient: answer B.

hints.title: Replace the repeated expressions
hints.body: Write X=2x, Y=log2y and Z=log2z. Rewrite all three equations using X, Y and Z.
hints.recap: This turns the system into linear equations.
hints.pitfall: Translate y>1 as well as z>0 into restrictions on the new variables.
hints.pause: Write the allowed values of X, Y and Z beside your equations.

recall.reminder: Keep the allowed range when you introduce a new variable.

hints.title: Subtract the last equation
hints.body: Subtract the third equation from the first, then from the second.
hints.recap: The matching terms cancel and leave one unknown in each new equation.
hints.pitfall: Check separately any k-value that would make you divide by zero.
hints.pause: Find X and Y in terms of k.

recall.reminder: Subtract equations to eliminate shared terms.

hints.title: Use the restrictions you wrote down
hints.body: Solve the inequalities needed for X and Y to have their allowed signs. Take the overlap.
hints.recap: The third equation can then give Z.
hints.pitfall: You must also be able to recover x, y and z from the new variables.
hints.pause: Find the full k-range and check that every value in it gives an original solution.

recall.reminder: Mark numerator and denominator zeros when solving a rational inequality.
